findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body: After invoking the disposer returned by `attach`, subsequent messages still invoke `handler`. Repeated attach/dispose cycles retain stale handlers and duplicate processing; restore `socket.off("message", handler)`.

findings.title: [P2] Restore interval cancellation in the polling cleanup
findings.body: After invoking the disposer returned by `startPolling`, `refresh` continues every second. Repeated lifecycles accumulate timers, and an active interval can prevent a Node.js process from exiting.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned teardown no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. After disposal, messages still invoke stale handlers; repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate duplicate listeners and retain associated state.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore interval cancellation in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned teardown no longer stops polling. The callback continues running after disposal, repeated starts accumulate concurrent intervals, and in Node.js the live interval can prevent process termination.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned cleanup function, subsequent `"message"` events still call `handler`. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles therefore retain stale handlers and can duplicate processing.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the interval in the polling disposer
findings.body:
Invoking the returned cleanup function leaves the interval active, so `refresh` continues after teardown indefinitely. In Node.js, the live interval can also prevent the process or test runner from exiting.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore socket listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
On a long-lived socket, disposing a session or subscription no longer removes its handler. Subsequent untrusted messages still execute stale handlers, and repeated attach/dispose cycles retain closures and amplify message processing, enabling memory/CPU exhaustion when connection churn is attacker-influenced.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval in the disposer
findings.body:
Every call now creates a permanent interval retaining its callback. In a long-lived process where polling lifecycles can be repeatedly initiated, including through attacker-driven requests or session churn, intervals accumulate indefinitely and can exhaust CPU and memory despite callers invoking cleanup.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
